limitations.text: All projections, forecasts and forward-looking statements in the 2026 Global Outlook are explicitly hypothetical and ‘should not be considered indicative or a guarantee of future results.’ The authors note that actual outcomes may differ materially from those expressed because of numerous unknown risks and uncertainties.

Historical relationships (for example, between market concentration and future equity returns) are acknowledged to be an ‘imperfect guide’; the report warns that timing the market based on concentration alone could have led investors to miss years of strong gains.

Simulated return benefits from adding private assets rely on Morningstar’s modelling framework and PitchBook indexes; the authors concede that higher fees, lower transparency and liquidity frictions could negate the modelled performance edge enjoyed in back-tests.

The report repeatedly stresses that markets are unpredictable and that 2026 may bring ‘a wide range of outcomes’, implying that portfolio recommendations are contingent on macro-economic scenarios that could quickly change.

Data used for indexes and back-tests are ‘gathered from reliable sources’ but Morningstar ‘cannot guarantee its accuracy, completeness, or reliability’, introducing potential measurement error into the analysis.
